title: A hidden leak in solids
abstract: Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02133-3 Solid electrolytes have long been treated as materials that block electronic conduction while enabling fast lithium-ion transport. Two studies now show that residual electronic conductivity can drive self-discharge in solid-state batteries at open circuit, particularly in thin practical cells, and identify the limits needed to ensure long shelf life.

title: Halogen-assisted sulfur oxidation
abstract: Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02086-7 <mark>Lithium-sulfur</mark> batteries have long been limited by lower operating voltage and shorter lifetime compared to traditional lithium-ion technologies. Now, system-level engineering enables the conversion of sulfur to disulfur dichloride, accessing the S+1 oxidation state, thereby delivering higher voltage and improved cycling stability.

title: Lithium–disulfur dichloride batteries
abstract: Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41560-026-02120-8 Rechargeable Li–S batteries offer high <mark>energy density</mark> but are limited by low voltage, sluggish kinetics and polysulfide shuttling. Here the authors report a chlorine-mediated Li||S2Cl2 chemistry enabling reversible three-electron sulfur redox with increased voltage and capacity.

title: Additive-assisted quasi-dry process enabling freestanding <mark>sulfide electrolyte</mark> films for <mark>all-solid-state</mark> batteries
abstract: Published online: 10 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77590-1 Thin <mark>sulfide electrolyte</mark> film could raise <mark>energy density</mark> of solid state battery, but producing thin, highly conductive film remains difficult. Here, authors develop an α-pinene assisted quasi-dry process to improve film quality and demonstrate a pouch cell retaining 83% capacity after 1000 cycles.
